channels.name: Direct operations
lines: Our own people run the floor, on our phones. They are the operators and a Portfolio Manager.
We do all of the steps below ourselves.

channels.name: Delivery partner
channels.who: The partner, on our phones, following our standards
lines: The partner hires their own team. The partner runs that team on our phones. They deliver the finished hours to us.
They sign the standard agreement. They follow every step below. Nobody skips a step.

phases.title: At the end of the month

steps.title: Find the site
steps.done: We have booked a meeting with a person who can say yes.
lines: We keep a list of the kinds of places we want to film in. We rank the list by task type. The task types we need more of go first. We also think about how the footage will get out of the site.
We contact sites through people we know. We also walk in and ask.
If you bring a site and the site signs, you get a 10% referral reward. Portfolio Managers also find sites for their own books. They earn the same reward.

steps.title: Sign the deal
steps.who: Mano handles the paperwork. Moharam handles the operational details.
steps.done: The agreement is signed. Access is confirmed. Mano has the payment terms.
lines: We meet the owner. We walk the floor. We agree what we film and what we pay.
We sign the participation agreement. We also agree on signage and consent.
We set the access hours and who may enter. We set the site's safety rules.

steps.title: Visit the filming location
steps.who: Mazen, Moharam, and the site's Portfolio Manager
steps.done: We have a plan for the site. The plan says where we record, where the power is, where the gear is kept, how the footage gets uploaded, and the shift pattern.
lines: We walk the whole site. We decide where we record and where we never record. We find where the power is. We decide where the gear is kept.
We confirm how the footage gets uploaded. Either the site has its own fiber, or a runner takes the footage to one of our hubs.
We agree the safety rules for that floor. We agree the protective gear for that floor.

steps.title: Central planning
steps.done: We have a dispatch schedule. It says which phones leave inventory on which day, and which site they go to.
lines: Central planning reads the dashboard. The dashboard shows how many floors are active, when each project ends, when phones and people come free, and how many workers are free.
From that, central planning writes the dispatch schedule. For example: take 40 phones from inventory on day X, and send them to the site on day Y.
Central planning sends the order to procurement. The order lists the phones, the caps, and everything else the site needs.

steps.title: Provide and hand out the gear
steps.done: The Portfolio Manager has every phone, cap, and mount that is on the schedule.
lines: Mazen gets the order from central planning. He provides the phones, the caps, the mounts, the chargers, and the spares.
He hands the gear to the site's Portfolio Manager on the day the schedule says.
Then the Portfolio Manager screens every worker. Nobody puts on a phone before they are screened.

steps.title: Screen every worker
steps.done: Every wearer has their papers on file. Every wearer has one account in their own name.
lines: The site suggests the person. The Portfolio Manager approves them.
We take a copy of their ID. They sign the consent form. They also sign to confirm they had the fraud briefing.
Each person has one account, in their own name. The account is never shared. The account is never reused.

steps.title: Day 0
steps.done: We have checked the pilot footage. Moharam has certified the launch.
lines: Set up the charging stations and the device room.
Label every phone and every mount. Test the network from the floor.
Show every wearer the camera angle. Show them the 30-minute cycle. Tell them this rule: before you take the hat off, tap stop first.
Record some pilot videos. Check the angle and the lighting. Do this before the first real hour.

steps.title: Film
steps.who: The Portfolio Manager and the operators
steps.done: The site records the hours it should, and the footage is clean, every day.
lines: Wearers change tasks. Nobody does the same task all week.
The wearers film in 30-minute cycles. The operators restart every cycle on time.
Every day, the operators charge the phones. They hand the phones over and sign for them. They clock in and clock out.
No phone keeps more than one day of footage overnight.

steps.title: Check on the site
steps.who: The Portfolio Manager, at any time
steps.done: The Portfolio Manager has visited the site today, at a time nobody expected.
lines: The Portfolio Manager visits the site without telling anyone first. They come at a different time each day.
In the first week after launch, they visit two or three times a day. In the second week, they visit one or two times a day. After that, they visit at least once a day.
On each visit, they check the camera angles, the 30-minute cycle, the charging, and custody. They also check how the wearers are doing.

steps.title: On-site quality control
steps.done: Every video has been checked on site before it uploads.
lines: At every 30-minute restart, the operator takes a quick look at the video that was just recorded. They check the angle, the lighting, and that the wearer is working.
At the end of the night, before anything uploads, every operator checks every video from their phones with care. They pull any video that must not go out.
The Portfolio Manager approves the day's footage. After that, the runner takes the phones.

steps.title: Upload
steps.who: The runner, sent by the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: Every phone has uploaded at a hub before the next shift starts.
lines: Most sites do not have fiber. So every night, the phones go to an upload hub. The phones upload over fiber at the hub.
There is one central hub downtown. There are two satellite hubs: one in Sheikh Zayed and one in the Fifth Settlement. A site uses the hub that is closest to it.
The runner takes the phones in several trips. The runner never puts all the phones in one vehicle. The runner brings the phones back before the shift.

steps.title: Quality control after the upload
steps.who: The quality control team with the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: The number of flags goes down every week. The client never gets a surprise.
lines: Our own team watches every video before the client sees it. For each video, they decide: keep it, flag it, or delete it.
A flag goes to the Portfolio Manager the same day. It goes to the worker within 24 hours, together with the fix.
If our reviewers give a worker three flags, the worker is pulled. If the client gives a second strike, the device is paused until the worker is retrained.
For every video the client flags as fraud, or bans for fraud, the operator and the Portfolio Manager pay a financial penalty.
Every day, the review corrects how we film.

steps.title: Report the number
steps.done: The number is on the dashboard every evening.
lines: Every Portfolio Manager sends the wrap report. The report has the hours, the active phones, the hardware, the problems, and the fixes.
Every evening, Mano combines all the reports into one company number.
The executive team checks every site against its quota. They move phones and people to the sites where the hours are. They resolve the day's escalations.

steps.title: Month-end audit
steps.done: The flagged footage is deleted. The clean total is agreed.
lines: We run every audit pass before we invoice anything.
We delete flagged footage. We never invoice it.

steps.title: Get paid for accepted hours, minus fraud flags
steps.done: Everyone in the chain is paid from the same number.
lines: The client pays for the hours it accepts.
Sites, workers, staff, and partners are all paid the same way, from the same number.
